correctness.rationale: The generating-disk and nearest-site inequalities give exactly three allowed polar angular-length branches, with changes at 1/2 and sqrt(2-sqrt(3)), and support endpoint 1/sqrt(3). Integrating 3rL(r)/A using exact primitives H and Q yields the elementary CDF and normalization. Alpha and Phi derivatives establish the 3/2-power onset, 24/A second-derivative jump and quadratic terminal tail. The standalone stdlib checker independently verifies original inequalities, derivatives, quadrature and sampled point frequencies; those finite computations are supporting evidence, not the proof. All region boundaries and zero-measure ties are handled.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The regular-polytope nearest-vertex gap theorem assumes flat faces and measures second-minus-first squared-distance, so its universal beta law does not imply the minimum on a nonpolygonal Reuleaux region. The polygonal-triangle point-picking formulas have the wrong domain and fixed-point statistic. The regular disk-triangle Steiner-area optimization concerns an outer parallel-body observable rather than clipped Voronoi cell areas.

value.rationale: Nearest distance to the three canonical generator vertices is the natural fixed-site quantization and three-disk coverage error of the Reuleaux triangle. The complete piecewise law reveals two geometrically distinct interior thresholds and distinct nonanalytic signatures; it is neither a routine area table nor an arbitrary parameter slice, and it makes exact coverage/risk probabilities available for the classical constant-width body. It is intrinsically useful without claiming an unproved extension.
